cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. This is a psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), and it's called a Maskil. David opens by telling us who's blessed, and he goes right to the subject of sin.

cards.question: In his opening line, who does David call blessed?

answers.text: The one whose transgressions are forgiven
The one who has never sinned at all
The one who keeps every command

cards.text: Then David says it a second way: blessed is the man whose iniquity the LORD does not count against him. That's the bill showing up stamped PAID IN FULL, and you never sent a dime!

cards.question: David says there is no deceit in the spirit of this blessed man, the one whose iniquity the LORD does not count against him.

cards.text: Now David gets personal and tells about a time he kept silent. Friend, that's putting tape over the check engine light and hoping the engine forgets.

cards.question: While David kept silent, what was it like for him?

answers.text: He rested easy all day long

cards.text: His bones became brittle from all that groaning. And David tells the LORD that day and night, the LORD's hand was heavy on him.

cards.question: With the LORD's hand heavy on him day and night, David says his strength held up just fine.

cards.text: His strength was drained as in the summer heat. That's me after twelve batches back to back by the ovens, melted down like a chocolate chip on a hot tray!

cards.question: Then something changed. David turned to the LORD and did not ___ his iniquity.
David says he will confess his transgressions to the LORD. What does the LORD do?

answers.text: He forgives the guilt of his sin
He lays a penalty on him
He turns His face from him

cards.text: David's told his own story, and now he says what it means for all the godly. He's that guy who taped over his check engine light, now telling EVERYBODY at work to go get theirs looked at!

cards.question: After what David went through, what does he want all the godly to do?

answers.text: Pray to the LORD while He may be found
Wait on the LORD until the storm has passed
Keep silent before the LORD in their trouble

cards.question: David pictures great waters rising, and he says they will not come near.

cards.text: Then David tells the LORD, "You are my hiding place." He quit hiding his iniquity and started hiding IN God, and friend, that beats the back of the junk drawer I spent years stuck in by a MILE!

cards.question: The LORD protects David from trouble and surrounds him with songs of ___.

cards.text: Then the psalm says, "I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go; I will give you counsel and watch over you." That's not getting handed a map and a "good luck," friend, that's getting watched over the WHOLE trip!

cards.question: Right after the line about being taught the way to go comes a warning: don't be like the horse or mule, which have no ___.

cards.text: They have to be controlled with bit and bridle to make them come. Friend, picture somebody yelling "WARM COOKIES in the break room!" and you still need a rope to get dragged in there. JUST COME!
Then the psalm sets two kinds of people side by side: the wicked, and the one who trusts in the LORD. I'm leaning in with my eyebrows up like a judge on a baking show, friend.

cards.question: The psalm says the wicked have only a few sorrows.
And the one who trusts in the LORD? What surrounds him?

cards.text: Last line, friend. David has a word for the righteous ones, the upright in heart, and I'm already dabbing my eyes with my mustache before he even says it.

cards.question: How does David call the righteous to respond to the LORD?

answers.text: Be glad and shout for joy
